ops.title: daemonkit verifies peers in the kernel: Security.framework leaves the handshake path entirely
ops.body:
Decision for the redesign's one gating open question, made by research rather than by the
originally-planned syspolicyd saturation test (yasyf, 2026-07-29: "just decide by reading and
searching the right thing to do"). Full document:
~/.claude/projects/-Users-yasyf-Code-daemonkit/cut/seccode/DECISION.md

## The decision

One `internal/trust` verifier reading the peer's status word, validation category, team
identifier, signing identifier, and DER entitlements blob via `csops_audittoken` against the
LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit token. **No Security.framework call on the handshake path at all.** The
disposable verifier child dies, the long-lived helper is not built, and in-process SecCode is not
shipped. No cache, no budget share, ~microseconds, load-independent.

## The measurement that decided it

Code-signing identity is a property of the IMAGE, not the path, and daemonkit's designated
requirement carries no path predicate (`codeidentity/identity.go:52-56`). Measured on this box and
independently re-verified: `cp -R` a Developer-ID-signed app to a user-writable path, and both
`codesign --verify -R='<daemonkit's exact DR>'` and every `csops` field (status word, identity,
team, validation category) come back **byte-identical to the original**.

Consequences, all load-bearing:

1. A same-EUID process needs NO signing capability whatsoever — only read access to the app you
   already shipped — to present a peer satisfying the full DR from a filesystem it controls.
   `/Applications/fuse-t.app` is installed on this machine.
2. So an in-process `SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes` opens a file whose location the attacker
   chose. On a wedged userspace mount that read is uninterruptible, pinning its M forever — an
   unkillable DoS primitive, and `wire/server.go:405-418` runs the handshake inline on the accept
   loop, so it wedges every accept.
3. Query-time certificate revocation was never a defense here. An attacker who can read your app
   already holds a binary satisfying your DR; revoking your certificate changes nothing.

Neither the shipping design nor the in-process candidate ever actually prevented this.

## Net security effect

**Strengthened**, on four axes: the six injection-entitlement rejections become unconditional
(today `trust/verify_darwin.go:340` exempts `disable-library-validation` when the status word
proves LV, and `codeidentity` — the verifier on the launchd install path — checks no entitlements
at all); validation category is a predicate neither verifier ever checked; the status word is
interpreted in exactly one place (`csposture.Check`, unmodified) so transcription divergence
cannot re-form; and the two-verifier P0 `7059185` closes with one implementation.

**Weakened**, on exactly one: `certificate leaf[subject.OU] == teamID` is no longer checked in
userspace, and is delegated to AMFI's exec-time binding of the CodeDirectory team identifier to
the leaf certificate's OU. Near-certain (Apple's own `defaultDeveloperIDLWCR` is
{ValidationCategory, SigningIdentifier, TeamIdentifier}, and library validation compares team
identifiers in-kernel) but NOT PROVEN. This is now the design's one gating measurement.

## What replaces task 12

**G1** — ~30 minutes, one signed binary, no load generation, no risk to the machine. With a real
Developer ID identity for team A, sign a binary whose CodeDirectory declares a foreign
teamID/identifier, run it, read `CS_OPS_VALIDATION_CATEGORY` and `CS_OPS_TEAMID`. Category != 6 or
team reported as A confirms the binding and ships as specified. Category 6 with the foreign team
adds a cdhash-memoized, singleflight, off-handshake-path chain check supplying only that clause —
copies share a cdhash, so it cannot be amplified.

The old saturation measurement was both moot (`SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes` is not called) and
unrunnable as specified (it demanded a real machine under exactly the host-wide saturation K55's
remedy forbids).

## Why the long-lived helper is removed, not deferred

A helper forbidden from self-exec'ing `os.Executable()` must exec something, and the only
candidate is a new shipped, signed, versioned artifact per consumer: a third version axis (which
the design forbids), a second artifact/deploy surface, and a bootstrapping paradox where the
process that verifies peers must itself be verified. It is not ~300 lines; it is a second
lifecycle in a repo whose P0 disease is too many lifecycles.

## Costs accepted

An undocumented-syscall dependency (`sys/codesign.h` is absent from the SDK) and an ~80-line
stdlib ASN.1 parser, replacing ~60 lines of purego CoreFoundation dictionary walking. Guarded
structurally and fail-closed — entitlements require magic 0xfade7172, strings require an 8-byte
length header, status requires CS_VALID — and pinned per macOS release by gate G2.

## Gates that came with it

G1 (above, phase 0). G2: every consumer's real signed fixture admits on each supported macOS,
including one App-Translocated and one notarized-and-stapled — the per-release ABI pin. G3: the
union-policy audit, since adopting injection rejections onto the launchd fixed-app path would
reject an Electron or CEF app outright; the escape hatch may relax `allow-jit` and
`allow-unsigned-executable-memory` and nothing else. G4: `DAEMONKIT_TRUST_E2E` and
`scripts/trust-fixtures.sh` appear in no workflow, so **the signed-peer path is verified by nobody
today** and G2 is meaningless without a CI home for it.
